courses.title: Ganita — Ancient Mathematics
courses.description: Shunya, place value, geometry, infinite series and the mathematical traditions of India.

lessons.title: Baudhayana's Theorem (Sulba Sutra)
lessons.overview: Explore the geometric relation between the diagonal of a rectangle and its sides in the context of precise altar construction.
lessons.content: The Baudhayana Sulba Sutra describes a diagonal-cord construction equivalent to the relationship a² + b² = c². Learners examine the geometry, construction logic, and the way measurement problems led to algorithmic thinking.
takeaways: Relate the diagonal rule to right-triangle geometry
Connect ancient measurement practices with modern coordinate geometry
lessons.practical: Use a grid, coordinates and a ruler to verify several integer right triangles.
lessons.english_meaning: Explore the geometric relation between the diagonal of a rectangle and its sides in the context of precise altar construction.
lessons.historical_context: Visualize a right-triangle relation in the context of Sulba measurement.
lessons.modern_parallel: The lesson connects cord-based geometric construction to a relation equivalent to a² + b² = c². Modern notation is used here as an explanatory bridge, not as a claim that the original text used modern algebraic symbols.
lessons.source: Baudhāyana Śulbasūtra; geometric construction tradition. Modern relation a²+b²=c² is an explanatory notation, not the original notation.

checkpoint.question: What is the central focus of “Baudhayana's Theorem (Sulba Sutra)”?
checkpoint.explanation: This lesson focuses on Baudhayana's Theorem (Sulba Sutra). Use the surrounding historical context and activity to deepen the idea.

lessons.title: Shunya & Decimal Place Value
lessons.overview: Trace the transition of zero into an operational mathematical digit and understand place-value notation.
lessons.content: Brahmagupta's Brahmasphutasiddhanta (628 CE) records arithmetic rules involving zero, positive quantities and negative quantities. The lesson compares place-value notation with later positional number systems.
takeaways: Explain why positional notation scales efficiently
Distinguish a placeholder from a numerical zero
lessons.practical: Build a place-value table and convert numbers between decimal representations.
lessons.english_meaning: Trace the transition of zero into an operational mathematical digit and understand place-value notation.
lessons.historical_context: Brahmagupta describes arithmetic operations involving zero in the Brahmasphutasiddhanta.
lessons.modern_parallel: The modern decimal system depends on positional notation and a symbol for zero; the historical development involved multiple stages and should not be reduced to a single inventor story.
lessons.source: Brahmasphuṭasiddhānta (628 CE), especially its arithmetic rules involving zero; broader positional notation has a longer history.

checkpoint.question: What is the central focus of “Shunya & Decimal Place Value”?
checkpoint.explanation: This lesson focuses on Shunya & Decimal Place Value. Use the surrounding historical context and activity to deepen the idea.

lessons.title: Madhava's Infinite Series for Pi
lessons.overview: Learn how the Kerala school used infinite series to approximate trigonometric functions and π.
lessons.content: Madhava's work is associated with series expansions for sine, cosine and arctangent. A simple alternating series for π demonstrates how repeated approximation converges toward a mathematical constant.
lessons.practical: Write a small Python loop that computes successive approximations of π.
lessons.english_meaning: Learn how the Kerala school used infinite series to approximate trigonometric functions and π.
lessons.historical_context: Kerala-school mathematics is associated with series for sine, cosine and arctangent, which can be used to approximate π.
lessons.modern_parallel: Power-series methods are directly analogous to numerical approximation, while the historical attribution must be tied to surviving Kerala-school texts and later commentarial evidence.
lessons.source: Kerala mathematical-astronomical tradition; surviving evidence comes substantially through later reports because Madhava’s mathematical writings are not extant.

checkpoint.question: What is the central focus of “Madhava's Infinite Series for Pi”?
checkpoint.explanation: This lesson focuses on Madhava's Infinite Series for Pi. Use the surrounding historical context and activity to deepen the idea.

lessons.title: Pingala, Prosody & Binary Patterns
lessons.overview: Use Sanskrit prosody to explore combinatorial patterns, binary-like representations and recursive counting.
lessons.content: Pingala's prosodic analysis classifies long and short syllables and supports systematic enumeration. The lesson introduces binary patterns and combinatorics as a modern computational interpretation.
takeaways: Connect poetic metre with discrete structures
lessons.practical: Enumerate all 4-bit patterns with a simple program.
lessons.english_meaning: Use Sanskrit prosody to explore combinatorial patterns, binary-like representations and recursive counting.
lessons.historical_context: Pingala’s prosody provides a systematic setting for counting patterns of long and short syllables.
lessons.modern_parallel: A binary/combinatorial analogy is useful pedagogically, but the ancient prosodic system should not be equated wholesale with modern binary computing.
lessons.source: Piṅgala’s Chandaḥsūtra / Chandaḥśāstra tradition; binary-like enumeration is a modern mathematical interpretation of two-state metrical patterns.

checkpoint.question: What is the central focus of “Pingala, Prosody & Binary Patterns”?
checkpoint.explanation: This lesson focuses on Pingala, Prosody & Binary Patterns. Use the surrounding historical context and activity to deepen the idea.

courses.title: Khagola Shastra — Astronomy
courses.description: Celestial cycles, apparent motion, eclipses and mathematical astronomy.

lessons.title: Aryabhata & Earth's Rotation
lessons.overview: Study the moving-boat analogy used to explain apparent stellar motion.
lessons.content: Aryabhata describes how a moving observer can perceive stationary objects as moving in the opposite direction. The lesson uses this analogy to reason about daily apparent motion of the sky.
takeaways: Separate apparent motion from physical motion
Describe axial rotation as a model
lessons.practical: Create a simple observer/reference-frame diagram.
lessons.english_meaning: Study the moving-boat analogy used to explain apparent stellar motion.
lessons.historical_context: Aryabhata’s moving-observer analogy is often discussed when explaining apparent daily motion of the sky.
lessons.modern_parallel: Relative-motion reasoning is the modern parallel: apparent motion depends on the observer’s reference frame.
lessons.source: Āryabhaṭīya; the lesson focuses on the moving-observer analogy for apparent stellar motion.

checkpoint.question: What is the central focus of “Aryabhata & Earth's Rotation”?
checkpoint.explanation: This lesson focuses on Aryabhata & Earth's Rotation. Use the surrounding historical context and activity to deepen the idea.

lessons.title: Surya Siddhanta & Eclipses
lessons.overview: Explore mathematical models for celestial positions, calendars and eclipses.
lessons.content: The Surya Siddhanta is a classical astronomical text containing rules for timekeeping, planetary positions and eclipse calculations. Students compare model-based prediction with observation.
takeaways: Identify inputs needed for an astronomical model
lessons.practical: Model a simple Sun–Earth–Moon eclipse alignment.
lessons.english_meaning: Explore mathematical models for celestial positions, calendars and eclipses.
lessons.historical_context: Classical siddhanta astronomy uses computational rules for time, celestial positions and eclipse geometry.
lessons.modern_parallel: The modern parallel is model-based astronomy: define parameters, compute positions, then compare predictions with observation.
lessons.source: Sūryasiddhānta astronomical tradition; edition, date and transmission history are complex.

checkpoint.question: What is the central focus of “Surya Siddhanta & Eclipses”?
checkpoint.explanation: This lesson focuses on Surya Siddhanta & Eclipses. Use the surrounding historical context and activity to deepen the idea.

courses.description: History of Ayurveda, preventive routines and the surgical literature of Sushruta.

lessons.overview: Review historical descriptions of reconstructive procedures, instruments and surgical preparation.
lessons.content: Sushruta Samhita contains detailed descriptions of surgical instruments and procedures. The lesson treats these as historical evidence and separates documented practice from modern medical interpretation.
takeaways: Recognize the scope of the surgical literature
Distinguish historical claims from modern clinical practice

checkpoint.question: What is the central focus of “Sushruta's Shalya Tantra”?

lessons.title: Charaka & Preventive Routines
lessons.overview: Explore daily and seasonal routines described in classical Ayurvedic literature.
lessons.content: Charaka Samhita discusses maintaining health through routine, diet, activity and seasonal adaptation. Students analyze how historical preventive frameworks differ from evidence-based modern medicine.

courses.title: Sthapatya Veda — Architecture

lessons.overview: Understand subtractive construction and structural sequencing in rock-cut architecture.
lessons.content: The Kailasa temple at Ellora is an example of monumental rock-cut construction. Students map the subtractive process, load paths and visual symmetry before comparing them with modern construction planning.
takeaways: Use sketches to communicate structural ideas

lessons.overview: Study grid-based spatial organization and how cultural intent can coexist with practical planning.
lessons.content: Vastu texts use geometric grids and orientation frameworks. The lesson emphasizes interpretation, context, and the distinction between traditional design principles and empirically validated building performance.

lessons.overview: Learn how crucible steel production created a high-carbon material valued across historical trade networks.
lessons.content: Wootz describes a family of crucible-steel production traditions associated with South Asia. This lesson focuses on furnace logic, carbon control and the later scientific study of microstructure.
takeaways: Explain crucible steel as a process
Distinguish historical evidence from modern hype
lessons.practical: Draw a process diagram from ore to finished steel.

lessons.title: Delhi Iron Pillar & Corrosion
lessons.overview: Use the Iron Pillar as a case study in long-lived wrought iron and protective surface layers.
lessons.content: The Delhi Iron Pillar provides a historical case for studying wrought iron, phosphorus, environment and corrosion products. Students investigate how material composition and exposure influence passivation.

courses.description: Reasoning, evidence, debate structures and the conceptual study of matter.

lessons.title: Kanada & Paramanu Theory
lessons.overview: Read Vaisheshika ideas about atoms as an example of historical theorizing about matter.
lessons.content: Vaisheshika texts classify substances and argue that matter can be analyzed into extremely small units. Students compare philosophical atomism with modern atomic theory without treating them as identical scientific models.
lessons.practical: Build a two-column comparison of historical concepts and modern particle theory.
lessons.english_meaning: Read Vaisheshika ideas about atoms as an example of historical theorizing about matter.

lessons.historical_context: Historical context for Kanada & Paramanu Theory within the Darshana & Nyaya — Philosophy & Logic tradition.

lessons.title: Panini's Ashtadhyayi as a Rule System
lessons.overview: Explore how compact rules encode transformations and structured linguistic behavior.
lessons.content: The Ashtadhyayi organizes concise sutras and meta-rules. Modern computing comparisons are useful as analogies, especially for formal grammars and rule-based processing, but the historical system remains its own linguistic tradition.
takeaways: Compare formal grammar as an analogy

daily_wisdom.sanskrit:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते।
तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्॥ २.५०॥
daily_wisdom.iast: buddhi-yukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛta-duṣkṛte | tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam || 2.50 ||
daily_wisdom.translation: Possessed of wisdom, one abandons both good and evil; therefore devote yourself to yoga, for yoga is skill in action.

daily_wisdom.sanskrit: आ नो भद्राः क्रतवो यन्तु विश्वतः॥
daily_wisdom.iast: ā no bhadrāḥ kratavo yantu viśvataḥ ||
daily_wisdom.translation: May noble thoughts / good inspirations come to us from every side.

daily_wisdom.iast: karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana ||
daily_wisdom.translation: Your sphere is action, never the fruits of action.

daily_wisdom.sanskrit: विद्या ददाति विनयं विनयाद् याति पात्रताम्।
daily_wisdom.iast: vidyā dadāti vinayaṁ vinayād yāti pātratām |
daily_wisdom.translation: Learning gives humility; from humility comes worthiness.
